$comment: The app registry. One entry per app-on-a-platform.
Wikipedia is the shipped sample because it costs nothing to reproduce: no
account, no local build, no secrets. Delete this entry and the matching
public/walkthroughs/wikipedia directory to start from empty —
Never put a literal secret in this file. Use a $ENV_VAR placeholder in
auth.roles.<role>.password and set the variable in .env.local.

projects.name: Wikipedia
projects.description: The shipped sample: search, reading an article, and the revision history — walked live against the public site.
projects.longDescription: Included because anyone who clones this repo can re-run the walk and get comparable output: no account, no local build, no secrets. It also happens to be the clearest available example of the problem this tool addresses — Wikipedia makes drift visible by keeping every revision addressable and every change diffable, which a deployed application cannot do. Article text is available under CC BY-SA 4.0; this is a sample, not an affiliation.

projects.name: Openstage
projects.description: The deck platform behind present.humanquest.net — a gallery, scroll and slide decks, a share gate and an admin studio, walked against the local dev server.
projects.longDescription: Openstage turns a repository into a presentation: authors register decks, the gallery filters and groups them, and each deck renders as either a long-form scroll or a fixed slide deck. It is walked here because it is the app the Walkthrough pattern is demonstrated on at AI Tinkerers Doha Round 3 — and because it exercises the parts of this schema that Wikipedia cannot: an authenticated area, a draft/unlisted surface, and interactive controls that are features of a page rather than pages of their own.

admin.note: Unset in the local environment; see issues.json — the middleware gate fails open when it is missing.

projects.name: DoneOS
projects.description: One accountable execution system for human and AI work. Its MCP feature now follows a connection from app settings to a real task in Queue and an attributed Activity event.
projects.longDescription: DoneOS gives agents the same execution contract people use. The product walkthrough opens the real Connect settings, uses the official MCP SDK against a disposable emulator account, and shows the exact task appear in the Flutter Queue and Activity history. A separate terminal surface preserves the deeper generated-contract proof without replacing the app story.

projects.name: Inner Quest
projects.description: A private Personal OS spanning character, relationships, career and wellbeing. Its MCP walkthrough turns assessment-backed self knowledge into a private reflection.
projects.longDescription: Inner Quest brings goals, relationships, career, wellbeing and reading into one private Personal OS. The walkthrough starts with secure OAuth, retrieves an official CliftonStrengths profile with provenance, shows how the product converts those themes into testable practices, and closes the loop with an authenticated private reflection visible in My Reflections.
